valid.code: const map = { a: (x) => { let y = x; return y; } };
valid.name: module-scope const map with inline multi-statement arrow - pre-built, not flagged

valid.code: class X { static map = { a: (x) => { let y = x; return y; } }; }
valid.name: static class field map with inline multi-statement arrow - pre-built, not flagged
single-expression arrow body (not a BlockStatement) - not flagged

valid.code: function build(items: readonly number[]) { return items.map((x) => { let y = x; return y; }); }
valid.name: inline arrow callback argument, but call site is NOT inside a loop - not flagged

valid.code: const arr = [(x) => { let y = x; return y; }];
valid.name: bare array literal holding an inline arrow, not passed to any call - not flagged

valid.code: function handler(cb = (x: number) => x + 1) { return cb; }
valid.name: default-parameter value is a single-expression arrow (not a BlockStatement) - not flagged

valid.code: function build() { return { a: (x) => { let y = x; return y; } }; }
valid.name: one-shot factory: map rebuilt inside a function body, but the function has no lexical loop position and no evidence of being called per-iteration - NOT flagged, same reasoning as `inlineFunctions`' identical redesign

valid.code: class X { field = { a: (x) => { let y = x; return y; } }; }
valid.name: non-static instance field rebuilds per instantiation, but instantiation is not loop iteration - not flagged

valid.code: function build() { return { handler: (x) => { let y = x; return y; } }; }
valid.name: suggestive key name "handler", no loop anywhere - not flagged; the gate is loop evidence, never the key's name

valid.code: function build() { return { transformAsync: (x) => { let y = x; return y; } }; }
valid.name: suggestive key name "transformAsync", no loop anywhere - not flagged, same reasoning

valid.code: function build(cond: boolean) { return { a: cond ? (x) => { let y = x; return y; } : (x) => { let z = x; return z; } }; }
valid.name: ternary-branched inline arrows as an object value, no loop anywhere - neither branch flagged

valid.code: function build(handler = (x: number) => { let y = x; return y; }) { return handler; }
valid.name: default-parameter multi-statement arrow closure whose owning function `build` is never called anywhere - not flagged, no evidence of call frequency at all

valid.code: function build(handler = (x: number) => { let y = x; return y; }) { return handler; } build();
valid.name: default-parameter multi-statement arrow closure whose owning function IS called, but the call site is not per-iteration - not flagged, call exists but is not proven hot

valid.code: declare const items: readonly number[]; declare function doWork(x: number): number; declare function process(it: number, cb: (x: number) => number): void; for (const it of items) { process(it, (x) => { const y = doWork(x); return y; }); }
valid.name: per-iteration arrow whose body is the explicit-return-binding house style (const y = <call>; return y;) - the pair collapses to one effective statement, not flagged

invalid.code: declare const items: readonly number[]; declare function process(it: number, cb: (x: number) => number): void; for (const it of items) { process(it, (x) => { let y = x; return y; }); }
invalid.name: inline arrow callback argument passed directly to a call inside a for-of loop - flagged (the textbook per-iteration-closure-allocation case)

invalid.code: declare function hasNext(): boolean; declare function process(cb: (x: number) => number): void; while (hasNext()) { process((x) => { let y = x; return y; }); }
invalid.name: inline arrow callback argument inside a while loop - flagged

invalid.code: declare function hasNext(): boolean; declare function register(entries: readonly [string, (x: number) => number][]): void; while (hasNext()) { register(Object.fromEntries([["a", (x) => { let y = x; return y; }]])); }
invalid.name: non-literal dispatch-table construction (Object.fromEntries) inside a loop - flagged

invalid.code: declare function hasNext(): boolean; declare function register(entries: Map<string, (x: number) => number>): void; while (hasNext()) { register(new Map([["a", (x) => { let y = x; return y; }]])); }
invalid.name: non-literal dispatch-table construction (new Map) inside a loop - flagged

invalid.code: declare const items: readonly number[]; function processItems(): void { items.forEach((item) => { const dispatch = { a: (x: number) => { let y = x + item; return y; } }; dispatch.a(1); }); }
invalid.name: dispatch-map value rebuilt inside an Array.prototype.forEach callback - flagged: migrating onto LoopContext (resolved via CallIdentity, not name-matched) closes the .forEach-shaped bypass a lexical loop-keyword walk would miss

invalid.code: declare function hasNext(): boolean; function build(cond: boolean) { while (hasNext()) { const map = { a: cond ? (x: number) => { let y = x; return y; } : (x: number) => { let z = x; return z; } }; void map; } } void build;
invalid.name: ternary-branched inline arrows as an object value in a map rebuilt every iteration of a real loop - both branches flagged

invalid.code: declare function hasNext(): boolean; function build(handler = (x: number) => { let y = x; return y; }) { return handler; } while (hasNext()) { build(); }
invalid.name: default-parameter multi-statement arrow closure whose owning function's ONLY call site is inside a loop - flagged, call-site reachability proves per-iteration allocation

invalid.code: declare function hasNext(): boolean; function build() { while (hasNext()) { const map = { transformAsync: (x: number) => { let y = x; return y; } }; void map; } } void build;
invalid.name: suggestive key name "transformAsync" inside a real loop - flagged identically to any other key name, no name-based escape

invalid.code: declare const items: readonly number[]; declare function doSomething(): void; declare function other(): number; declare function process(it: number, cb: () => number): void; for (const it of items) { process(it, () => { doSomething(); return other(); }); }
invalid.name: two genuinely distinct statements (an unrelated call, then a different return) - no collapse, still flagged

invalid.code: declare const items: readonly number[]; declare function doWork(x: number): number; declare function sideEffect(): void; declare function process(it: number, cb: (x: number) => number): void; for (const it of items) { process(it, (x) => { const y = doWork(x); sideEffect(); return y; }); }
invalid.name: const y = <call>; sideEffect(); return y; - the trailing return collapses with nothing, since the immediately preceding statement (sideEffect()) is not its binding - still flagged
